input.quote: enter into a new subordination agreement with a new lender(s) on terms and conditions that are taken as a whole not less favorable in any material respect to SFJ than those set forth in the subordination agreement to be entered into with SVB
input.rationale: No most-favoured-nation covenant burdens PB anywhere in the Agreement. Full-text searches for "most favored/favoured", "no less favo(u)rable", "at least as favorable", "right of first refusal/negotiation" and "third party offer" returned only one hit (Section 7.4/p0543), which requires that any replacement subordination agreement be on terms not less favorable to SFJ than the SVB subordination agreement — a lien-priority/refinancing condition, not an obligation to extend SFJ any better commercial terms granted to a third party. The Licensing Transaction provisions (Section 7.5.5, p0552) give SFJ a limited consent right tied to "Material Impact" and arbitration, but again impose no obligation on PB to match or pass through third-party terms. This meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), so no redline is warranted.
